- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap next-day forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment drops sharply (≤0.25) and price falls, model underreacts; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast if sentiment <0.30.
- Model overestimates mean reversion in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral; adjust downward by 2–4% for short-term forecasts.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.30–0.75), model often misreads trend direction; align forecast slope with sentiment’s recent average direction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (first 5–7 days), reduce forecast peak by 5–8% to avoid overconfidence in long-term trend.
